articles.title: Gable Steveson Doesn't Belong in the UFC?
articles.description: The media is dancing on Gable Steveson's grave after a 12-second knockout, and Chael has had enough of it. In this video, Chael dismantles the narrative that Gable "doesn't belong in the UFC." The fight lasted exactly 12 seconds, the same duration as Jose Aldo versus Conor McGregor, and nobody ever said Aldo didn't belong. Gable had already won a fight in the UFC before this loss, proving he earned his spot. Chael draws a sharp comparison to Olympic boxing, where a gold medalist walks into the professional ranks in the top 10 with zero pro fights, which is essentially what Gable did transitioning to MMA. He revisits the bare-knuckle knockout that prompted Joe Rogan to text Dana White saying the whole division was in trouble, and reminds everyone that Gable has bounced back before, including from the biggest upset in wrestling history in the NCAA final in front of the President on ESPN. Chael's core argument is simple: nobody could have taken that shot, just like nobody could have taken what Masvidal did to Askren. But the real kicker is this, not one UFC fighter under contract has called Gable out, even though fighting him guarantees a main card spot, a press conference, and maximum attention. Everybody is certain he doesn't belong, yet nobody has asked for the shot. Whatever Gable does next, we're all going to be watching. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #GableSteveson

articles.title: Ilia Topuria’s 145 Return Isn’t Happening Yet #ufc
articles.description: Is Ilia Topuria going back to 145 pounds? Chael Sonnen has an emphatic answer: **not anytime soon.** Justin Gaethje recently suggested that Ilia is naturally a 145-pound fighter and argued that size could eventually become an issue for him at lightweight. But Chael believes Ilia’s mindset makes a return to featherweight extremely unlikely right now. According to Chael, Ilia won’t simply leave lightweight because the division is physically demanding. He believes Ilia will stay at 155 until he solves the problem—and that means winning the UFC lightweight championship. A return to 145 could still happen eventually, especially if it means a massive matchup with Alexander Volkanovski. But Chael believes there is one major condition: Ilia would first need to recapture the lightweight title. So forget about an immediate move back to featherweight. If Chael is right, Ilia Topuria is staying at 155. #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria #ChaelSonnen #UFC155 #UFC145 #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #UFCNews

articles.title: The real reason Chael Sonnen lost to Anderson Silva #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen reveals one of the strangest moments of his fighting career—and it happened because his corner told him the wrong round. Chael had never fought five rounds before, and as he entered the later stages of the fight, he was running on exhaustion, fear and urgency. His mindset was simple: get the takedown, stay busy and keep scoring. Then his corner told him it was the fourth round. The problem? It was actually the fifth. Suddenly, the urgency disappeared. Chael no longer believed he needed to keep attacking—he thought he still had another round to work. Instead of fighting to win, he was unknowingly fighting to beat the clock. Chael explains how that experience changed his perspective on five-round fights and why the mental side of championship rounds can be just as important as the physical exhaustion. Was it an excuse? articles.title: Should Arman Be Ranked Above Ilia?
articles.description: The new MMA Fighting rankings just put Arman Tsarukyan ahead of Ilia Topuria, and Chael is not sure they got it right. In this video, Chael breaks down one of the most surprising ranking debates in recent memory. Ilia Topuria is a two-division UFC champion in the two hardest weight classes in the sport, a feat only Conor McGregor had accomplished before. Chael argues that if not for paperwork, Ilia would have simultaneously held the featherweight, lightweight, and BMF titles. He compares Ilia's resume to Islam Makhachev's, noting both have one loss and two-division championships, and questions whether recency bias is clouding everyone's judgment. Chael also dives into the bizarre narrative that Topuria shouldn't even qualify for a title shot at the belt he held just five months ago. This is Chael at his best, using history, logic, and a little bit of mischief to challenge how we think about greatness. He asks fans to imagine looking back five years from now with fresh eyes: would you still rank Islam ahead of Ilia? It's a debate about paper versus perception, and Chael makes a compelling case that the rankings might be missing the bigger picture. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #IliaTopuria #ArmanTsarukyan

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan Is NOT Underestimating Gaethje #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan believed in Justin Gaethje when almost nobody else did—and Chael Sonnen says that could matter if they fight. Arman reportedly put $1 million on Gaethje to beat Ilia Topuria, showing just how highly he has rated Justin’s ability all along. That belief could become important in a matchup between the two. Chael explains why Arman is unlikely to make the same mistake other opponents have made: underestimating Gaethje. Justin’s ability to keep moving forward, absorb adversity and refuse to quit is one of his biggest weapons. Arman knows exactly what he’s dealing with. He knows Gaethje’s power, his leg kicks, his wrestling credentials and how difficult he is to control. That awareness could make this matchup completely different. Arman Tsarukyan believes in Justin Gaethje—and he knows exactly how tough he is. #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #UFCLightweight #IliaTopuria #MMA

articles.title: Gane Called Tom Aspinall Mentally Fragile
articles.description: Ciryl Gane just called Tom Aspinall "mentally fragile" to his face, and Chael thinks the insult might reveal something much deeper about why Aspinall hasn't returned. In this video, Chael presents a fascinating theory about the power of the subconscious mind in fighting. Using the story of a roofer who couldn't bring himself to climb back on the same roof where he fell, and John Stossel's famous WWF lawsuit where Stossel admitted he felt better the moment the settlement check arrived, Chael draws a parallel to Aspinall's situation. Aspinall is out with an eye injury, and his reward for healing is a rematch with Gane, a nightmare matchup he already knows too well. Chael also revisits Jon Jones's surprising decision to step away rather than face Aspinall, and Jones's backhanded compliment that there's not enough footage of Aspinall to even form a game plan. This isn't just fight analysis, it's psychology. Chael explores how the mind can protect the body by inventing reasons to stay out, and why Gane's accusation that Aspinall is using the eye poke as an excuse might be both cruel and accidentally insightful. Whether Aspinall is truly hurt or subconsciously avoiding the fight, the question remains: what happens when he has no choice but to return against Gane? Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #TomAspinall #CirylGane

articles.title: Why Would Morales Take This Fight?
articles.description: Michael Morales is one win away from fighting Islam Makhachev for the title, so why on earth did he just accept a fight with Ian Garry? In this video, Chael breaks down the high-stakes chess match happening at welterweight right now. Morales hasn't fought since November, stayed healthy, and stayed unbooked, which in the UFC usually means one thing: a title shot is coming. But after a heated back-and-forth with Ian Garry that spilled into the media, Morales said yes to a fight that could cost him everything. Chael explains the rumor about Dana White's whispered promise at Madison Square Garden, why the fans sided with another contender over Morales, and how Garry is the worst possible opponent to take right before a title fight. This is a masterclass in UFC matchmaking and risk management. Chael lays out why beating Garry does almost nothing for Morales, but losing to him ends the title dream instantly. It's the kind of fight that looks brave on paper and reckless in practice, and Chael isn't afraid to say so. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #MichaelMorales #IanGarry

articles.title: The Weirdest 4 Minutes in MMA
articles.description: Darren Till and Yoel Romero just stood nose-to-nose for four straight minutes, and Chael can't stop thinking about how bizarre the whole thing was. In this video, Chael breaks down the strangest face-off in recent memory, explaining why the staredown ritual exists in the first place and what really happens when the camera flashes finally stop. Drawing from his own fighting career, Chael admits he used to believe winning the face-off gave him an edge, until he realized it had absolutely no effect on the fight itself or how many people tuned in. He walks through the moment a UFC staffer finally taps you on the shoulder to end it, and the strange realization that once the lights stop flashing, that's just what you look like. This goes beyond Till and Romero. It's about the psychology of intimidation, the theater of fight promotion, and why two grown men get locked into a staring contest neither one can actually win. Chael's conclusion is blunt: once you're in it you might as well finish it, but don't lie to yourself that it means anything. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #DarrenTill #YoelRomero

articles.description: It's time for another Ask Uncle Chael, and this one goes everywhere. Chael starts with Hoofy's loss to Arman Tsarukyan and explains why one result shouldn't erase what a fighter actually showed in the cage. His message is simple: dust yourself off, let the loss go and start over with the next opponent. From there, Chael answers questions about Mayhem Miller, Johnny Cash, which UFC fighter could embrace being the bad guy, concerns surrounding artificial intelligence, relationships and, naturally, the best order at Burger King. articles.title: Alex Pereira Was Just Given His Next Fight #ufc
articles.description: Alex Pereira’s next fight may already be finalized—and Chael Sonnen thinks he knows exactly who it is. Chael explains why he believes Pereira is headed for a matchup with Alexander Volkov. Pereira was recently brought into the UFC offices, and according to Chael, fighters don’t get called in simply to hear an idea—they get brought in when something significant is being finalized. Pereira vs. Volkov would also make for a fascinating No. 1 contender matchup. Both are elite kickboxers, but Volkov brings a major size advantage and represents one of the challenges we’ve already seen create problems for Pereira at heavyweight. There’s also unfinished business surrounding Pereira, Ciryl Gane, and the ongoing heavyweight title picture. So is Alex Pereira vs. Alexander Volkov already done? articles.title: Should Oblique Kicks Be Banned in MMA?
articles.description: Andy Foster and Dana White have both raised concerns about oblique kicks, and Chael Sonnen agrees they deserve a serious look. Chael's standard is simple: if a technique is considered too dangerous to use on your training partners in the practice room, why should it automatically be acceptable in competition? Oblique kicks make that list. Unlike traditional leg kicks that accumulate damage over the course of a fight, Chael argues the oblique kick is specifically designed to hyperextend the knee and potentially cause an immediate, long-term injury. But he doesn't stop there. Chael brings up two other techniques he believes deserve the same scrutiny: heel hooks and 12-to-6 elbows. He explains what Randy Couture once told him about the danger of heel hooks and questions why MMA recently brought the 12-to-6 elbow back into competition. Where should MMA draw the line between effective technique and unnecessary injury risk? CHAPTERS: 00:00 Should oblique kicks be banned? 00:36 The practice room test 01:45 Heel hooks are just as dangerous (Randy Couture's warning) 02:56 The three most dangerous techniques in MMA 03:31 The oblique kick is designed to hyperextend the knee 04:12 Damage is the government's number one criterion 05:15 If you wouldn't do it in practice, ban it from competition Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@sonnen?sub_confirmation=1

articles.title: Gable Steveson Forgot What Made Him Great#ufc
articles.description: Gable Steveson didn’t lose because he suddenly became a bad fighter. Chael Sonnen believes he lost because he stopped doing what made him special. Chael breaks down the biggest lesson Gable needs to take from the fight: wrestle. For an elite wrestler, simply getting your hands on an opponent can completely change the fight. You don’t necessarily need a takedown. Get connected, control the arms or waist, and force the opponent to deal with your greatest skill set. Instead, if Gable starts obsessing over every striking mistake and trying to fix everything at once, Chael believes he could miss the real lesson. “Gable’s a wrestler. In the future, wrestle.” Chael explains why abandoning your first skill set can be like spotting an opponent 10 years of experience—and why Gable’s path forward may be much simpler than people think. #UFC #MMA #GableSteveson #ChaelSonnen #Wrestling #MMAWrestling #UFCNews #MMATraining #WrestlingToMMA

articles.title: Is Topuria Too Small for Lightweight?
articles.description: Justin Gaethje believes Ilia Topuria belongs back at 145 pounds. Chael Sonnen's response? No. It's not that Topuria could never return to featherweight. Chael believes there's one thing that would have to happen first: Ilia would need to finish his business at lightweight and recapture the 155-pound title. Chael explains why fighters like Topuria don't change divisions to escape a problem, why moving back to featherweight now would go against the mentality that got Ilia this far, and what Alexander Volkanovski's pursuit of a second championship can teach us about the psychology of fighting with another belt still waiting at home. Could Topuria vs. Volkanovski happen again at 145? Chael loves the matchup. He just doesn't believe Ilia will entertain it until he has accomplished what he set out to do at lightweight. CHAPTERS: 00:00 Will Topuria go back to 145? 00:16 Gaethje started this debate 00:37 A fighter will never cut weight to run 01:30 Only after he recaptures the 155 title 01:41 The Volkanovski lesson at 155 02:37 Topuria vs Volkanovski is fascinating 02:45 Gaethje knows size matters 03:30 145 or 155, you weigh the same thing 04:19 I like the idea of Ilya vs Volkanovski 04:31 Save yourself the breath Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@sonnen?sub_confirmation=1

Will Gaethje Fight Again?
articles.description: Justin Gaethje says he's taking the rest of 2026 off to enjoy being champion, and that decision could completely change what his next fight looks like. Chael Sonnen breaks down Gaethje's comments on the lightweight division, including his belief that Ilia Topuria belongs back at featherweight and that Arman Tsarukyan could beat him. But there's another possibility: while Gaethje waits, the contenders beneath him may have to fight each other. Tsarukyan, Paddy Pimblett and Topuria could all have very different situations by the time Gaethje is ready to return. The opponent who makes the most sense today might not even be available when the UFC finally makes the call. Chael explains why Gaethje's decision to wait could put him in an unusually powerful position and why predicting his next opponent right now may be impossible. articles.title: Volkov is happy for "Mentally Ill" Josh Hokit
articles.description: Chael Sonnen has had a problem with Alexander Volkov for years, but it's actually a compliment. Volkov has done almost everything right. He's fought the best heavyweights in the world, stepped up as one of the UFC's earliest backup fighters, and Chael still believes Volkov beat Ciryl Gane despite losing the decision. The problem? He's never consistently demanded what he deserves. That may finally be changing. After seeing Volkov take aim at Josh Hokit and then digging through some of his older comments, Chael realized there's another side to Volkov that fans rarely get to see. He's funny, creative and understands how to get people talking. Now Chael wants him to take that personality away from social media and put it where it matters most: on the microphone. Josh Hokit has shown exactly how powerful that can be. Chael explains why Volkov should take notice and start playing the promotional game that could finally push him toward a UFC heavyweight title opportunity. CHAPTERS: 0:00 Volkov struck again 0:45 The first backup fighter in UFC history 1:52 You can win a fight and lose the decision 2:21 Why Volkov annoys Chael: he won't grab the mic 3:14 Volkov booked in Abu Dhabi 3:53 The Nate Marquardt one-leg story 5:51 Hokit's whole schtick: he has something to say 6:39 Volkov's comments about Hokit 7:26 Ryan sends Chael old Volkov clips: he's hilarious 8:34 Final advice: take it to the microphone #UFC #MMA #AlexanderVolkov Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@sonnen?sub_confirmation=1

articles.title: The Day in MMA: Jones–Cormier Brawl Got Its Bill  | Sept 23
articles.description: The Day in MMA: Jones–Cormier Brawl Got Its Bill September 23, 2014. Seven weeks after Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier went off the stage and into the MGM Grand lobby, Nevada handed down the price: Jones $50,000 and 40 hours of community service, Cormier $9,000 and 20 hours. No suspensions. Unanimous vote. Jones admitted under questioning that the brawl cost him his Nike deal. Cormier's answer: "I didn't lose a Nike deal. I didn't have one." Twelve years ago today. articles.title: Jon Jones vs Daniel Cormier: The Brawl, The Hearing & The $50,000 Fine (12 Years Ago Today)
articles.description: Jon Jones vs Daniel Cormier: The Brawl, The Hearing & The $50,000 Fine (12 Years Ago Today) On September 23, 2014, the Nevada Athletic Commission ruled on the UFC 178 media-day brawl between Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier. Hours before the Aug. 4 face-off, Cormier told MMA Weekly he would "attack him the whole time." Then the two men touched foreheads on stage, Cormier shoved, Jones swung, and both went off the stage into the MGM Grand lobby. Eight days later Jones withdrew injured and UFC 178's main event collapsed — but Nevada still wanted answers. At the hearing, Jones told commissioners "I made us all look bad… as a man I sit here to accept them," and admitted the brawl cost him his Nike sponsorship. Cormier argued self-defense — "a reaction to him putting his head on mine" — and said he had no Nike deal to lose. The commission's ruling: no suspension for either man. Jones was fined $50,000 with 40 hours of community service; Cormier $9,000 with 20 hours. The motion passed unanimously. Outside the room, Cormier called it fair. They finally fought at UFC 182 on January 3, 2015. Jones won by unanimous decision.
